content: Melvin-Koushki says Ibn Turka follows that passage with a catalogue of statements by the righteous salaf, notably Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal and al-Shāfiʿī, who in upholding the uncreated Quran defend the eternality of its every letter; Zamakhsharī's failure to appreciate the virtue of the quranic letters is singled out for censure, and the interlude ends by exhorting the ‘less intelligent and more fractious’ to hold to the way of the pious forebears and the folk of the Sunna.
refers_to_primary: Ibn Turka, Mafāḥiṣ, MS Majlis 10196 ff.89b-90a (per MK fn.150)
